tools.name: search_games
tools.description: Find browser games by player preferences. Returns at most 10 (default 3) ranked games with direct play links, match reasons and evidence labels. Strict filters never accept unknown facts; check "shortage" when fewer games match than requested.

tools.name: get_game_details
tools.description: Return the authoritative public catalog record for one game id from search_games: every fact with its evidence method, source and date (or "unknown"), developer attribution, link status and play URL, plus `related`: up to 8 similar games (shared genre, sub-genre, style, theme and tone, later also wh

tools.name: start_sign_up
tools.description: Start an optional Hocus Games account for a person who asked for it, with ONLY their email address and, optionally, the genres, graphics styles, themes and tones they want to hear about. We email them a confirmation link; they confirm, choose their password and accept the Terms of Service on the Hoc

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "start_sign_up" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Start an optional Hocus Games account for a person who asked for it, with ONLY their email address and, optionally, the genres, graphics styles, themes and tone…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_game_details, start_sign_up · Private data: get_game_details, start_sign_up · Public sink: start_sign_up.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_game_details, start_sign_up · Private data: get_game_details, start_sign_up · Public sink: start_sign_up

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
